title: Pet Science
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 16S/24Q to fewer than 30S/45Q units

outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of the various species of pets, pet management systems, and the different industry opportunities associated with the respective species.
Understand the scientific principles of animal production in relation to genetics, reproduction, nutrition, physiology, and environment.
Demonstrate competency in the areas of animal health, disease, welfare and handling and understand how these factors influence animal stress and welfare.
Demonstrate knowledge of the economic influence of the pet industry in today's society.

Be competent with the use of technology and have abilities in the areas of critical thinking and decision-making. In addition, they must have strong oral and written communication skills, and a sense of the importance of responsibility and work ethic.

notes: Outcomes come from the page's Outcomes tab for Pet Science (Certificate N0630), headed 'Program Learning Outcomes'.
The second outcome is preceded in the source text by an invisible zero-width space character, which was omitted.
The closing line 'Review Student Learning Outcomes (SLOs) for this program.' is a link, not an outcome, and was not recorded.
The 'Total Units 16' line is printed for the whole course list, which is also the certificate total, so it was recorded as total_units rather than as the block's stated total.
